This section defines the shared calculation contract for the offshore wind
infrastructure model. The model evaluates one complete user-supplied case
deterministically; it does not optimize or select a preferred design.

## Calculation Logic

For each case, the model:

1. validates the user inputs and fixed parameters;
2. constructs the wind-farm layout and gross production;
3. selects the electricity, centralised-hydrogen or
   decentralised-hydrogen component chain;
4. calculates physical inventories, component sizing, losses and auxiliary
   demand;
5. returns an explicit infeasible or not-parameterized status when a required
   constraint or input is unresolved;
6. applies annual subsystem availability once at architecture level;
7. aggregates non-overlapping capital and operating costs; and
8. reports the carrier-specific energy and cost outputs.

Electricity and hydrogen are delivered at different onshore interfaces. Their
costs may be shown side by side, but they are not equivalent end-use service
prices.

## Methodology Pages

Read the shared method in dependency order:

1. [System Boundary and Carrier-Cost Metrics](system_boundary_and_lcoe.qmd)
   defines the endpoints, cost boundary and reported units.
2. [Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions](financial_and_price_basis.qmd)
   defines EUR 2025 normalization and annual cost.
3. [Inputs, Parameters and Outputs](optimisation_variables.qmd) defines the
   deterministic model record.
4. [Modelling Workflow](modelling_workflow.qmd) defines the execution order and
   failure states.
5. [Energy and Availability](energy_availability_and_annualisation.qmd) defines
   the energy basis and architecture availability ledger.

Component pages own their physical equations, component-specific assumptions,
evidence and non-overlapping CAPEX and OPEX.
